title: ipw: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights
text: ipw package provides flexible toolkit estimating Inverse Probability Weights (IPW) fit marginal structural models. Functions estimate probability receive observed treatment, based individual characteristics. inverse probabilities can used weights estimating causal effects observational data via marginal structural models. point treatment situations longitudinal studies can analysed. functions can used correct informative censoring.

title: ipw: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights
text: Point Treatment & Longitudinal Data: Functions handle static exposures time-varying confounding. Wide Range Models: Support binomial, multinomial, ordinal, continuous (Gaussian) exposures. Survival Analysis: Integration Cox proportional hazards models time--event data. Diagnostic Tools: Built-plotting functions assess weight stability positivity assumption.

title: ipw: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights
text: example simulates data continuous confounder (l) binomial exposure () estimate marginal causal effect 10.
code: library(ipw) library(survey)  # 1. Simulate data set.seed(123) n <- 1000 simdat <- data.frame(l = rnorm(n, 10, 5)) a.lin <- simdat$l - 10 pa <- exp(a.lin)/(1 + exp(a.lin)) simdat$a <- rbinom(n, 1, prob = pa) simdat$y <- 10*simdat$a + 0.5*simdat$l + rnorm(n, -10, 5)  # 2. Estimate IPW weights temp <- ipwpoint(    exposure = a,    family = "binomial",    link = "logit",    numerator = ~ 1,    denominator = ~ l,    data = simdat)  # 3. Fit Marginal Structural Model (MSM) msm <- svyglm(y ~ a,                design = svydesign(~1, weights = ~temp$ipw.weights, data = simdat))  summary(msm) #>  #> Call: #> svyglm(formula = y ~ a, design = svydesign(~1, weights = ~temp$ipw.weights,  #>     data = simdat)) #>  #> Survey design: #> svydesign(~1, weights = ~temp$ipw.weights, data = simdat) #>  #> Coefficients: #>             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> (Intercept)  -6.2885     0.2757  -22.81   <2e-16 *** #> a            10.6622     0.8083   13.19   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 22.76977) #>  #> Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2

title: ipw: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights
text: longitudinal research, HIV cohort haartdat, ipwtm calculates cumulative product weights time.
code: library(ipw) library(survival)  data(haartdat)  # Estimate time-varying weights for HAART initiation temp_tm <- ipwtm(   exposure = haartind,   family = "survival",   numerator = ~ sex + age,   denominator = ~ sex + age + cd4.sqrt,   id = patient,   tstart = tstart,   timevar = fuptime,   type = "first",   data = haartdat )  # Visualize weight stability ipwplot(weights = temp_tm$ipw.weights, timevar = haartdat$fuptime,          binwidth = 100, main = "Stabilized Weights Over Time")

title: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights (Point Treatment) — ipwpoint
text: exposure Name exposure column data (unquoted string). Binomial exposure variables coded 0/1. family Model family exposure: "binomial", "multinomial", "ordinal", "gaussian". link Link function binomial ("logit", "probit", "cauchit", "log", "cloglog") ordinal ("logit", "probit", "cauchit", "cloglog"). Ignored multinomial gaussian. numerator Formula specifying right-hand side numerator model. NULL, unstabilized weights (numerator = 1) calculated. denominator Formula specifying right-hand side denominator model. data Data frame containing exposure model covariates. trunc Optional truncation percentile 0 0.5 (e.g., 0.01 1st/99th percentiles). ... Additional arguments passed model fitting functions (glm, multinom, polr).

what: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights (Time Varying) — ipwtm
title: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights (Time Varying) — ipwtm
text: Estimates inverse probability weights fit marginal structural models time-varying exposures time-varying confounders across follow-intervals. Supports binomial, survival, multinomial, ordinal, gaussian families.

title: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights (Time Varying) — ipwtm
code: ipwtm(   exposure,   family = c("binomial", "survival", "multinomial", "ordinal", "gaussian"),   link = NULL,   numerator = NULL,   denominator,   id,   tstart,   timevar,   type = c("first", "cens", "all"),   data,   corstr = "ar1",   trunc = NULL,   ... )

title: Estimate Inverse Probability Weights (Time Varying) — ipwtm
text: exposure Name exposure column data (unquoted string). family Model family: "binomial", "survival", "multinomial", "ordinal", "gaussian". link Link function binomial ordinal models. numerator Formula numerator model. NULL, unstabilized weights computed. denominator Formula denominator model. id Name subject identifier column data. tstart Name interval start time column (required family = "survival"). timevar Name follow-(interval end) time column. type Exposure switch type: "first", "cens", "". data Data frame containing required variables. corstr Correlation structure GEE family = "gaussian" (default: "ar1"). trunc Optional truncation percentile 0 0.5. ... Additional arguments passed model fitting engines.

initiation of HAART therapy on mortality. #Estimate inverse probability weights to correct for confounding. #Exposure allocation model is Cox proportional hazards model. temp <- ipwtm(   exposure = haartind,   family = "survival",   numerator = ~ sex + age,   denominator = ~ sex + age + cd4.sqrt,   id = patient,   tstart = tstart,   timevar = fuptime,   type = "first",   data = haartdat)  #plot inverse probability weights graphics.off() ipwplot(weights = temp$ipw.weights, timevar = haartdat$fuptime,         binwidth = 100, ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5), main = "Stabilized inverse probability weights")  #CD4 count has an effect both on dropout and mortality, which causes informative censoring. #Use inverse probability of censoring weighting to correct for effect of CD4 on dropout. #Use Cox proportional hazards model for dropout. temp2 <- ipwtm(   exposure = dropout,   family = "survival",   numerator = ~ sex + age,   denominator = ~ sex + age + cd4.sqrt,   id = patient,   tstart = tstart,   timevar = fuptime,   type = "cens",   data = haartdat)  #plot inverse probability of censoring weights graphics.off() ipwplot(weights = temp2$ipw.weights, timevar = haartdat$fuptime,         binwidth = 100, ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5),         main = "Stabilized inverse probability of censoring weights")  #MSM for the causal effect of initiation of HAART on mortality. #Corrected both for confounding and informative censoring. #With robust standard error obtained using cluster(). require(survival) summary(coxph(Surv(tstart, fuptime, event) ~ haartind + cluster(patient),               data = haartdat, weights = temp$ipw.weights*temp2$ipw.weights)) #> Call: #> coxph(formula = Surv(tstart, fuptime, event) ~ haartind, data = haartdat,  #>     weights = temp$ipw.weights * mortality. #Longitudinal CD4 is a confounder as well as intermediate for the effect of TB.  #process original measurements #check for ties (not allowed) table(duplicated(timedat[,c("id", "fuptime")])) #>  #> FALSE  #>  6291  #take square root of CD4 because of skewness timedat$cd4.sqrt <- sqrt(timedat$cd4count) #add TB time to dataframe timedat <- merge(timedat, basdat[,c("id", "Ttb")], by = "id", all.x = TRUE) #compute TB status timedat$tb.lag <- ifelse(with(timedat, !is.na(Ttb) & fuptime > Ttb), 1, 0) #longitudinal CD4-model require(nlme) #> Loading required package: nlme cd4.lme <- lme(cd4.sqrt ~ fuptime + tb.lag, random = ~ fuptime | id,                data = timedat)  #build new dataset: #rows corresponding to TB-status switches, and individual end times times <- sort(unique(c(basdat$Ttb, basdat$Tend))) startstop <- data.frame(   id = rep(basdat$id, each = length(times)),   fuptime = rep(times, nrow(basdat))) #add baseline data to dataframe startstop <- merge(startstop, basdat, by = "id", all.x = TRUE) #limit individual follow-up using Tend startstop <- startstop[with(startstop, fuptime <= Tend),] startstop$tstart <- tstartfun(id, fuptime, startstop) ifelse(with(startstop, !is.na(Ttb) & fuptime > Ttb), 1, 0) #indicate death startstop$event <- ifelse(with(startstop, !is.na(Tdeath) & fuptime >= Tdeath),                           1, 0) #impute CD4, text: ipwpoint(): weights.trunc wrong whenever trunc set. lower upper quantiles recycled across rows, every truncated weight replaced one two bounds. Weights now clipped trunc 1 - trunc quantiles, weights bounds left unchanged. ipwtm() family = "multinomial" "ordinal": predicted probabilities now matched observed exposure level name rather column position. 1.3.1 stopped error two-level exposure, exposure level occur among rows used fit models. ipwpoint() family = "multinomial" now works two-level exposure; 1.3.1 stopped error (“Observed exposure levels match fitted probability levels”). Added test unstabilized weights (numerator) family = "multinomial" "ordinal" ipwpoint(). failed 1.3.0 fixed 1.3.1 rewrite (#3, @adcascone). ipwtm() type = "first" family = "multinomial" / "ordinal": switch defined first record level lowest level whole data set, ipw <= 1.2.1.1. 1.3.1 reference level chosen separately subject.

title: ipw 1.3.2
text: ipwtm() now checks model variables exist contain missing values, binomial/survival exposure coded 0/1, clear error messages instead errors inside glm() / coxph(). ipwtm() family = "survival" now stops clear message formula contains strata(), supported. Fitted models returned num.mod / den.mod longer carry inlined copy data call, printing readable . ipwpoint() ipwtm() share one set internal helpers argument checks, formula construction, probability extraction truncation. Removed blanket import() whole packages; calls use pkg::fun. methods longer imported.

title: ipw 1.3.2
text: Test suite expanded: exact checks truncation, row-order invariance, two-level multinomial vs binomial equivalence, error messages. New regression test ipw 1.2.1.1 (reference weights created data-raw/make-regression-fixtures.R).

title: ipw 1.3.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-30 Improved defensive input validation, parameter checking, error messages across core functions. Modernized formula construction (.formula()) eliminate fragile eval(parse(text = ...)) string manipulations. Fixed variable symbol evaluation issues passing variables function arguments rather raw names. Modularized ipwtm dedicated family modeling engines (binomial, survival, multinomial, ordinal, gaussian). Replaced manual survival hazard step-differencing continuous baseline hazard interpolation using survival::basehaz stats::approx. Refactored tstartfun use safe column evaluation direct vector lag logic (c(-1, t[-length(t)])). Upgraded testthat suite 3rd edition specs, expanding coverage multinomial, ordinal, gaussian, unstabilized models, weight truncation, invalid parameter rejection.
